tokenEvents.label: User access token

claims.scope: ai:agent:read transfer read openid records:read write

tokenEvents.explanation:
Issued by PingOne after Authorization Code + PKCE login. Stored in the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) session (server-side httpOnly cookie — never sent to the browser). Token carries 6 scope(s): ai:agent:read transfer read openid records:read write
✓ Agent scopes: ai:agent:read

claims.scope: ai:agent:read transfer read openid records:read write

tokenEvents.label: ID token (OpenID Connect)
tokenEvents.explanation: Issued by PingOne at login when the openid scope is granted. Proves the user's identity to the BFF (the relying party): aud is the BFF client_id, and claims like auth_time and acr describe how and when the user authenticated. Held in the BFF session and used for OIDC sign-off — it is NOT a bearer for API calls (that is the access token above) and never reaches the browser.

tokenEvents.label: Refresh token (RFC 6749 §1.5)
tokenEvents.explanation: Issued by PingOne at login when the offline_access scope is granted. An OPAQUE credential (not a JWT — no claims to decode) used to silently mint new access tokens when the current one expires (RFC 6749 §6). Held server-side in the BFF session and never sent to the browser; the token value is intentionally not shown here.

tokenEvents.label: User Token — PingOne Active-Token Introspection at Login (RFC 7662)

claims.scope: ai:agent:read transfer read openid records:read write

tokenEvents.explanation: PingOne confirmed the user token is active at login. sub=1aee74ae-3d09-4bcf-a69f-7e1bc225b761 scope="ai:agent:read,transfer,read,openid,records:read,write". Introspection is called once per login and cached in the session.

claims.scope: ai:agent:read transfer read openid records:read write

tokenEvents.label: Token exchange (RFC 8693): user access token → MCP access token
tokenEvents.explanation: Your session has a user access token (above). The exchange runs when the AI Agent invokes a banking tool. For high-value and transfer transactions, the exchange is paired with human-in-the-loop consent (HITL).

tokenEvents.label: MCP access token (delegated) → MCP server
tokenEvents.explanation: After a successful exchange on an MCP tool call, decoded MCP access token claims (including act, audience, and scope) appear here.

responseBody.description: Banking Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) acts as MCP Host for the browser: session cookie auth, optional RFC 8693 token exchange, then WebSocket JSON-RPC to the MCP server.

bff.title: MCP Host — Backend-for-Frontend (BFF), browser / React
bff.audience: End users signing in through the web app.
bff.pingOneOAuth: Authorization Code + PKCE → tokens stored in httpOnly server session on the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF). Browser does not hold access tokens for MCP.
bff.tokenExchange: RFC 8693 token exchange before MCP: narrow scopes + MCP audience + act/delegation (configured).
bff.mcpClientTransport: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) opens WebSocket JSON-RPC (initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/list / tools/call).
bff.bestForShowing: PingOne + OAuth for humans, session-bound tokens, and why exchange + least privilege protect backends from the browser.

langchain.title: MCP Host — LangChain (AI agent)
langchain.audience: Autonomous chat agent and MCP client in Python.
langchain.pingOneOAuth: Client credentials (ai_agent) for the agent; user context via CIBA / session flows as designed — not the React session cookie.
langchain.tokenExchange: Target pattern: exchange user/agent context for MCP-scoped tokens (see ARCHITECTURE.md); complements Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) for non-browser actors.
langchain.mcpClientTransport: WebSocket to MCP with Bearer on connect; chat UI uses separate WebSocket (port 8080).
langchain.bestForShowing: How an AI agent acts as MCP client, uses tools, and still reaches the same MCP server that enforces introspection and scopes.

shared.mcpServer: Same banking_mcp_server: initialize, tools/list, tools/call → validates tokens (PingOne introspection), scopes, then Banking REST API.
shared.bankingApi: Banking API remains behind Bearer validation + scope checks — not called directly from the browser for MCP tool execution.

flow: 1. User authenticates → OAuth tokens stored in httpOnly session on the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF).
2. Discovery: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) sends initialize + tools/list over WebSocket to MCP server.
3. Execution: LLM or Inspector selects a tool → Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) sends tools/call with delegated token when configured.
4. MCP server introspects token, checks scopes, calls Banking API with Bearer token — backend stays behind MCP + API auth.
